statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-25680 (GO-2026-5028, GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw) is excessive CPU use in the golang.org/x/net/html parser, fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5028, https://go.dev/issue/79573, fix https://github.com/golang/net/commit/08be507abce89191d78cd49da60f4501fc910472). The fix changes only html/parse.go (the parser's addFormattingElement), and the advisory's vulnerable symbols are html.Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and parser.parse. Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, on both x86_64 and aarch64: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 through 0.35.0-r2, each downloaded and checked against the index checksum. Each package holds two regular files, usr/bin/alertmanager and usr/bin/amtool, both statically linked Go programs built with CGO_ENABLED=0; the two architectures agree in every build. golang.org/x/net is v0.49.0 to v0.53.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.32.1-r1 and v0.55.0 to v0.62.0 from 0.32.1-r2. A search of the Go function-name strings of both binaries in every build finds golang.org/x/net/html functions only in 0.35.0-r0 to 0.35.0-r2; no earlier build contains any golang.org/x/net/html function. In 0.35.0-r0 to 0.35.0-r2 (x/net v0.62.0), the function table (pclntab entries and inlined names) of both binaries, on both architectures, holds only the html tokenizer in alertmanager (html.NewTokenizerFragment and Tokenizer methods) and only html.init in amtool; none of the parser functions above is present. Positive control: the same two searches on a CGO_ENABLED=0, -ldflags=-w test program that calls html.Parse with x/net v0.62.0 find html.Parse, html.ParseWithOptions and html.(*parser).parse. The vulnerable parser code is therefore not present in any published build.

CVE-2026-25680 (GO-2026-5028, GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw): parsing arbitrary HTML with the golang.org/x/net/html parser can consume excessive CPU time, possibly leading to denial of service. The vulnerable code is Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and the parser's parse method in the golang.org/x/net/html package (the functions GO-2026-5028 lists), fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5028, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw, https://go.dev/issue/79573, https://go.dev/cl/781702, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8. We read every published build-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 91 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64 (2.6.4-r0 is published for aarch64 only), after verifying each download against its index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times for each architecture in the package index; the one copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one program, the Go frontend program /usr/bin/build, besides the apk metadata. For every Go program in every build we read the function table (pclntab) and searched the binary's strings; each program's function table contains runtime.main. No build contains golang.org/x/net/html code: the golang.org/x/net packages linked into /usr/bin/build are http/httpguts, http2, http2/hpack, idna, internal/timeseries and trace, and none of the parser functions above appears in its function table or its strings. As a check, the same function-table reader lists ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and the parser's parse method, and the same strings search finds all five names, in a test program built against golang.org/x/net v0.54.0 for x86_64 and aarch64. The vulnerable code is not present, so the golang.org/x/net version recorded in the build information does not make this package affected.

Debian lists this CVE as no-dsa for golang-golang-x-net in trixie; this decision rests on our own scan of the shipped binaries, not on that status. We downloaded every published kube-state-metrics-dev package for Alpine 3.23 from the DHI Alpine repository, 2.18.0-r0 to 2.20.0-r13 (28 versions, 54 packages: x86_64 and aarch64, except 2.20.0-r7 and 2.20.0-r8, which are published for aarch64 only), each checked against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/kube-state-metrics, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its build information lists the golang.org/x/net module (v0.48.0 to v0.53.0 up to 2.18.0-r6, v0.55.0 to v0.62.0 from 2.19.0-r0 on), but in none of the 54 binaries does the Go function table (read from .gopclntab) contain any function of the golang.org/x/net/html package, and a byte search of every binary finds no golang.org/x/net/html symbol name, so neither the functions listed above nor the addFormattingElement code the fix changes is present. The golang.org/x/net packages the program does link, in every build, are bpf, http/httpguts, http/httpproxy, http2, http2/hpack, idna, internal/httpcommon, internal/timeseries, trace and websocket. As controls, the function table of every one of these binaries lists runtime.main, and the same function-table read finds 91 golang.org/x/net/html functions, including the parser's parse and addFormattingElement methods, ParseWithOptions and ParseFragmentWithOptions, in test programs built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/net v0.54.0 that call all four exported functions; the same byte search finds all five listed names there (Parse and ParseFragment are inlined into their caller, so they appear only as strings). Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5028, https://go.dev/issue/79573, the fix https://github.com/golang/net/commit/08be507abce89191d78cd49da60f4501fc910472 and https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 27 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (50 packages). Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies); we read the whole program from every package. Its Go build information lists golang.org/x/net, with no replacement and the same on both architectures: v0.53.0 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.20.4-r2, v0.54.0 in 1.20.4-r3 to 1.20.4-r4, v0.55.0 in 1.20.4-r5 to 1.21.0-r1, v0.56.0 in 1.21.0-r2 to 1.21.0-r3, v0.57.0 in 1.23.1-r0 to 1.23.1-r1, v0.58.0 in 1.23.1-r3 to 1.23.1-r6, v0.59.0 in 1.23.1-r8 to 1.23.1-r10, v0.61.0 in 1.26.0-r1 to 1.26.0-r3, v0.62.0 in 1.26.0-r4 to 1.29.0-r0 and v0.63.0 in 1.29.0-r1 to 1.30.0-r0. Reading the program's Go function table in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control) shows that the only golang.org/x/net/html symbols are the package initializer and its mathMLAttributeAdjustments table: no build has html.Parse, html.ParseFragment, html.ParseWithOptions, html.ParseFragmentWithOptions or html.(*parser).parse, and a byte search of every build, which also finds the names of functions the compiler inlined, finds no 'html.(*parser).parse'. The HTML parser is not in the program, so the vulnerable code is not present, whichever x/net version a build carries. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search, run on a test program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and -trimpath for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/net v0.53.0 that calls html.Parse, find html.Parse and html.(*parser).parse in both the function table and the byte search. The CVE is open in Debian 13 (trixie), where its golang-golang-x-net package is marked no-dsa (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-25680); this decision rests on the code in these builds, not on that status.

GO-2026-5028 (CVE-2026-25680, GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw): in golang.org/x/net/html, parsing crafted HTML can consume excessive CPU time and cause a denial of service. The vulnerable code is the HTML parser: the advisory's affected symbols are Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and parser.parse, fixed in golang.org/x/net 0.55.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5028, https://go.dev/issue/79573, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8. Checked /usr/bin/trivy, the only file in every published trivy-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository (0.69.1-r0 to 0.74.0-r12, 38 builds each on x86_64 and aarch64), each verified against the repository index checksum, reading its Go build information (go version -m) and its Go symbol table (go tool nm). Each is a statically linked Go program for Linux, built with CGO_ENABLED=0. The builds up to 0.70.0-r3 carry golang.org/x/net 0.50.0 to 0.54.0, inside the affected range, and the builds from 0.70.0-r4 carry 0.55.0 to 0.63.0. In every build the symbol table holds exactly one function of package golang.org/x/net/html, its package initializer golang.org/x/net/html.init; none of the parser functions the advisory lists, and no other parser or tokenizer function or method, is in the binary (functions of the separate golang.org/x/net/html/charset package are linked; that package detects character encodings and is not the parser). A search of the raw bytes of /usr/bin/trivy in every build, which would also find the names of inlined functions, finds none of the listed function names, while it finds runtime.main and golang.org/x/net/html.init in each. As a control, the same symbol and byte searches on a program built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/net 0.54.0 that calls html.Parse and html.ParseFragmentWithOptions find ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and (*parser).parse.

CVE-2026-25680 (GO-2026-5028): Parsing arbitrary HTML can consume excessive CPU time, possibly leading to denial of service. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/net/html package and is fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5028, https://go.dev/cl/781702, https://go.dev/issue/79573, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/net packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/net package. In no published build is golang.org/x/net/html among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, amd64 and arm64), together with the oci-config and debug-symbol (dbgsym) packages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/net/html directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/net/html code or symbols. The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Debian security repository for Debian 13 hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog, and no program. The only occurrence of the string golang.org/x/net/html in any program is an example import path in the help text of go list, built into the go command. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/net/html takes it from its own golang.org/x/net requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/net in that program.

CVE-2026-25680 (GO-2026-5028, GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw): parsing arbitrary HTML with the golang.org/x/net/html package can consume excessive CPU time, possibly leading to a denial of service. The functions GO-2026-5028 lists are Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and the parser's parse method in golang.org/x/net/html. The fix, commit 08be507 in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0, changes only html/parse.go: it adds an attrCompare helper and sorts element attributes so that the parser's addFormattingElement method compares them with slices.Equal. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5028, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw, https://github.com/golang/go/issues/79573, https://github.com/golang/net/commit/08be507abce89191d78cd49da60f4501fc910472 and https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8. Debian lists this CVE as no-dsa for golang-golang-x-net in trixie; this decision rests on our own scan of the shipped binaries, not on that status. We downloaded every published kube-state-metrics-dev package for Debian 13 from the DHI Debian repository, 2.18.0-5 to 2.20.0-13 (23 versions, 44 packages: amd64 and arm64, except 2.20.0-7 and 2.20.0-8, which are published for arm64 only), each checked against the repository's SHA-256 checksum except the amd64 2.20.0-4 package, whose served file does not match the checksum in the repository index; we read the file the repository serves, which reports Go 1.26.8 and golang.org/x/net v0.58.0. The amd64 package of 2.20.0-4 that the repository serves does not match its index checksum (the same size, the same different SHA-256 on repeated downloads); we read the served file. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/kube-state-metrics, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its build information lists the golang.org/x/net module (v0.53.0 up to 2.18.0-6, v0.55.0 to v0.62.0 from 2.19.0-0 on), but in none of the 44 binaries does the Go function table (read from .gopclntab) contain any function of the golang.org/x/net/html package, and a byte search of every binary finds no golang.org/x/net/html symbol name, so neither the functions listed above nor the addFormattingElement code the fix changes is present. The golang.org/x/net packages the program does link, in every build, are bpf, http/httpguts, http/httpproxy, http2, http2/hpack, idna, internal/httpcommon, internal/timeseries, trace and websocket. As controls, the function table of every one of these binaries lists runtime.main, and the same function-table read finds 91 golang.org/x/net/html functions, including the parser's parse and addFormattingElement methods, ParseWithOptions and ParseFragmentWithOptions, in test programs built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/net v0.54.0 that call all four exported functions; the same byte search finds all five listed names there (Parse and ParseFragment are inlined into their caller, so they appear only as strings). The vulnerable code is not present, so the golang.org/x/net version recorded in the build information does not make this package affected.
